**W7**: "Yes. When the right moment came to get rid of him, he was too sharp for them." — "him" has no antecedent in the window. "Tommy said Tuppence softly" then "Yes" — the "him" being discussed is unknown. Also the opening "Yes" is a connective response to something not in the window.

**W8**: Opens with "Yes. When the right moment..." — same issue as W7, this is the second paragraph of that content. "Why?" is the first paragraph here — the "why" responds to something not in the window (connective dangle).

**W19**: Opens with "A vague alarm stirred in Tuppence..." — this is a mid-scene continuation but stands reasonably. The "Quite right, Miss Tuppence. You scent danger" — Sir James's eyes upon her then he speaks. This flows from W18 but W19 itself has "Sir James's eyes upon her" establishing enough. Acceptable.

**W30**: "Sir James looked from one to the other, longest at Tommy. 'You,' he breathed." — "Tommy" is a named character (fine), but this window opens with Julius having said his line, then Sir James looks at Tommy — "Tommy" appears with no prior establishment in this window as present in the scene.

**W32**: Opens with "You! I might have known." — "They relaxed their hold a fraction." — "they" has no antecedent in this window.

**W33**: "They relaxed their hold a fraction" — same "they" issue carries into this window too, but W33's first paragraph has "they" from W32.

**W1**: "Sir James's words came like a bomb-shell." — "He set a clipped paragraph before Jane" — this "He" refers to Sir James, established by name in same sentence. Fine. "As I was saying to Miss Tuppence" is a callback dangle.

**W29**: "As he did so, an iron grip seized him" — "he" and "him" have no antecedent in this window (the person raising the gun is not named here).

**W31**: Opens mid-dialogue "You! I might have known." — no context for who is speaking to whom or what the revelation is. "Sir James looked from one to the other" — "one to the other" implies two people whose identities aren't established.
